answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 220 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The pearl graph is validated at intake and the signal frontier is published, which means the ancestry of every answer is public, and vertex anchors the chain at a checkpoint. The bill scales 15 fold, not the vote. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
